round: independent-review F1-F5 remediation, review baseline b48dc44d519c1d2813dabd33e5a85a50e7f8da9c
items: F2: start snapshot, generated-class-only write set, conflict preservation
F3: pre-checked targets, limited write set with backups and a bounded undo
F5: mandatory and complete PGV scope enforcement at the strict generation entry

three_trees.start_snapshot: snapshotRoots() records every managed root's content when generation begins; it is the only baseline the comparison uses
three_trees.staged_output: the throwaway copy the templates write into, plus the repository's own OpenAPI post-processing
three_trees.pre_write_working_tree: re-read per target immediately before writing, solely to decide whether the user moved anything while generation ran

write_set.rule: only files in the generated classes the chain can emit may be written: *.pb.go, *.pb.validate.go, *.pb.redact.go and the single app/admin/service/cmd/server/assets/openapi.yaml; anything else under an output root is hand-written and is never a target
write_set.why_not_a_whole_directory_rule: pkg/localdeps/go-wind-toolkit/protoc-gen-go-redact holds 28 hand-written files (main.go, fields.go, redact/v1/interface.go, tests, .proto, .md, LICENSE) next to the one generated redact/v1/redact.pb.go, and the assets directory holds the hand-written go:embed assets.go next to openapi.yaml; an output-root rule is what overwrote the reviewer's interface.go
write_set.classification_test: TestGeneratedArtifactClasses plus TestEveryCommittedArtifactUnderAManagedRootIsClassified, which counts the hand-written files that must survive the sweep per root (api/gen/go 0, go-crud 0, kratos-bootstrap 0, assets 1, redact package 28)

conflicts.generated_artifact_moved: refusal: the error names the file, nothing in the batch is written, and the user's content stays on disk
conflicts.hand_written_file_moved: never in the write set, so it cannot be clobbered; the run reports "preserved hand-written edit" and continues
conflicts.non_generated_file_created_or_changed_by: refused as an unmanaged write target, because a template writing outside its classes is a defect, not something to propagate

design.full_chain_sweep: sweepGenerated() deletes every generated-class file from the staged copy before a full-chain run, so previous output cannot be carried into the comparison and passed off as a rebuild; hand-written files stay so they are not mistaken for losses. A partial run keeps its seeded copy and is judged only on what it actually writes, which is what keeps it from being required to produce all 103 validators

scope.mandatory: readPGVScope fails on a missing file, unreadable file, corrupt JSON, no entries key, empty entries, a duplicate entry, an empty or escaping or absolute validator path, and a validator_count that disagrees with the entries; approvedValidators() returning "nil means no rule" is gone
scope.complete_output_check: the scope is applied to the whole validator output of the run, not only to additions: a validator in the write set must be approved whether it is new or already in the tree and being rewritten, an approved artifact the chain did not produce fails a full run, and an approved artifact missing from the tree fails too
scope.no_count_inflation: the 103-entry list, the parked model template, the plugin pins and the five-feature Ent contract are unchanged; nothing was deleted from the tree to make a comparison pass and no plugin response is filtered

design.limits_stated: the rollback is a bounded undo of one write-back: it does not promise whole-directory atomicity under a power loss or a kill between two renames, and no general transaction layer was built

rollback.before_any_write: every destination is inspected for path and type conflicts, and needed parent directories are created; a directory or symlink on a destination path fails the run before the first byte moves
rollback.during: each file being replaced is copied to a temporary backup directory outside the tree, and after each rename the destination digest is compared with the staged digest
rollback.on_failure: files this run replaced are restored from the backups and files this run added are removed, newest first, and directories this run created are removed while still empty
rollback.user_content_after_us: a file whose current content is not what this run wrote is left completely alone and named in the report, so the undo cannot overwrite a newer user edit
rollback.failed_rollback: reported as its own condition: the message says the rollback is incomplete and the tree is not restored, names each file it could not undo, and preserves the backup directory instead of deleting it
rollback.not_used: no git checkout, git reset or whole-tree restore anywhere in the tool; the injected faults live only in a throwaway worktree
